claims.value: Government forces defeated the liberal regular army at Palonegro; the war subsequently relied more heavily on guerrillas.

scope.description: Named historical constitutional government and source-dated wartime action; no assertion of uniform territorial control or modern nationality.

evidence.locator: De sangre y llanto un río; rendered lines 34 and 39; La guerra Continúa, line 46
evidence.note: Palonegro lasted 11–26 May 1900 and ended in liberal defeat.

qualifications: Date is the battle conclusion, not a claim that the entire war ended. Casualty estimates omitted.

claims.value: Conservative conspirators overthrew Sanclemente and installed Vice-President José Manuel Marroquín.

scope.description: Named historical constitutional government and source-dated wartime action; no assertion of uniform territorial control or modern nationality.

evidence.locator: El golpe de Marroquín y esperanzas de paz; rendered lines 42–43
evidence.note: The coup took place on 31 July 1900.

qualifications: Dated change in executive authority; no assertion that peace followed or that the constitutional framework changed.

scope.description: Named historical constitutional government and source-dated wartime action; no assertion of uniform territorial control or modern nationality.

evidence.locator: War: Antecedentes inmediatos, line 30; presidents: Sanclemente and Marroquín entries, lines 1008–1029
evidence.note: Sanclemente assumed personally on 3 November 1898; Marroquín replaced him on 31 July 1900.

evidence.locator: War: Antecedentes inmediatos, line 30; presidents: Sanclemente and Marroquín entries, lines 1008–1029
evidence.note: Sanclemente assumed personally on 3 November 1898; Marroquín replaced him on 31 July 1900.

qualifications: Research coverage starts at the existing entity envelope in 1899. Nominal presidency began 7 August 1898; acting Marroquín served until 3 November.
Half-open interval ends at the sourced 31 July 1900 transition; no invented separate 30 July departure.

scope.description: Named historical constitutional government and source-dated wartime action; no assertion of uniform territorial control or modern nationality.

evidence.locator: José Manuel Marroquín entry and Período; rendered lines 1018–1029

qualifications: Coverage ends within the existing wartime entity envelope; actual presidency continued to 7 August 1904.
Wartime executive office is distinguished from effective territorial control.
